slo_title: Explain how signed numbers are multiplied using Booth’s algorithm.

mcq.q: Why does Booth’s algorithm use arithmetic right shifts after each step?

options.A: To double the value of the product
options.B: To ensure the sign bit is preserved during shifts
options.D: To add the partial products directly

mcq.answer_text: To ensure the sign bit is preserved during shifts

mcq.q: Which of the following is an advantage of Booth’s algorithm over basic shift-and-add multiplication? A) B) C) D) Answer: B

options.B: It reduces the number of addition/subtraction operations for certain multiplier patterns
options.C: It is only for unsigned numbers
options.D: It eliminates the need for shifting

mcq.answer_text: It reduces the number of addition/subtraction operations for certain multiplier patterns
